funding: Mainly public: City of Kamloops, Province of BC, BC Arts Council, Canada Council, TNRD, plus Vancouver, Audain and Hamber foundations, named individual donors and local corporate sponsors; BCLC sponsors free Thursday admission.
why_flagged: BCLC, which the Cullen Commission found ignored money-laundering warnings until 2015, sponsors free Thursday admission.
other_findings: The Cullen Commission (June 2022) found BCLC ignored repeated law enforcement warnings about casino money laundering until 2015 and called its risk tolerance 'completely unacceptable and unreasonable'.

bottom_line: The gallery is mainly publicly funded and names its donors. The one item worth watching is BCLC's sponsorship of free admission, given the Cullen Commission's findings about BCLC. No reporting found of protest or criticism aimed at the gallery itself.

funding: Privately funded non-profit with no published funder list; it is housed in Ilham Tower, controlled by the family of the late Daim Zainuddin through Ilham Baru Sdn Bhd.
why_flagged: The gallery's building, owned by the Daim family, is under MACC seizure and forfeiture proceedings that the owners are challenging in court.
other_findings: MACC seized Ilham Tower on 18 December 2023 under the MACC Act, in a probe tied to the Pandora Papers.
In June 2025 MACC re-seized the tower under the AMLATFPUAA 2001 and filed to have it forfeited, alongside orders on UK assets valued at about RM700M-758M.
Unverified: MACC alleges the assets are linked to offences under Section 4(1) of the AMLATFPUAA; Daim, who died in November 2024, denied wrongdoing and called the probe politically motivated.
On 4 November 2025 the High Court granted Ilham Tower Sdn Bhd leave to challenge the second seizure, with an interim stay on enforcing forfeiture.
bottom_line: No reporting found of wrongdoing by the gallery itself, but it has no public funder list. Its home and probable patron family are the subject of MACC seizure and forfeiture proceedings that are still under challenge in court; worth watching is the outcome of the forfeiture case.
